title: Canon 9: meditation on hell; Liber II corona — consensus of confessions — Cap. 15 / Liber II close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Next: PHYS 467 BOOK THREE Chapter 1. 15 / Liber II COMPLETE. Cap. || Closing distich belonging toward Bernard belonging toward Morlaix: No one can speak or write or meditate ye joys belonging toward ye just nor ye torments belonging toward ye wicked. For ye which ye God belonging toward peace stands as to be prayed such that he further confirm it. For ye rest: as concerning Sacred Scripture in Book I, so concerning man's highest good plus its opposite evil in Book II — among theologians against papist tyranny who embrace ye Augsburg, Helvetic, French, English, plus Belgian confessions, by God's benefit there stands as consensus. || It serves repentance plus consolation. Let us descend into hell while living lest we descend while dying (Bernard). in persecutions to comfort by confidence belonging toward eternal immunity. (9) Perpetual meditation on hell ought to rouse us out from ye flesh's security plus license to sin;
pass_b_english: (9) Perpetual meditation on hell ought to rouse us from the flesh's security and license to sin; in persecutions to comfort by confidence of eternal immunity. Let us descend into hell while living lest we descend while dying (Bernard). It serves repentance and consolation.

For the rest: as concerning Sacred Scripture in Book I, so concerning man's highest good and its opposite evil in Book II — among theologians against papist tyranny who embrace the Augsburg, Helvetic, French, English, and Belgian confessions, by God's benefit there is consensus. For which the God of peace is to be prayed that he further confirm it. Closing distich of Bernard of Morlaix: No one can speak or write or meditate the joys of the just nor the torments of the wicked.
source_text: 9. Perpetua inferni meditatio a carnis securitate & peccandi licentia nos excitare debet; in persecutionibus solari fiducia aeternae immunitatis. Descendamus in infernum viventes ne descendamus morientes (Bernardus). Facit poenitudini & consolationi. Caetera: quemadmodum de sacra Scriptura libro primo, ita de summo hominis bono & opposito malo libro secundo — inter Theologos adversus papisticam tyrannidem, Augustanam, Helveticam, Gallicam, Anglicanam & Belgicam confessionem amplexos, Dei beneficio consensus est. Quem ut Deus pacis porro firmet orandus est. Clausula Bernhardi Morlanensis: Nemo potest fari nec scribere nec meditari gaudia justorum necnon tormenta malorum. [Cap. 15 / Liber II COMPLETE. Next: PHYS 467 LIBER TERTIUS Cap. 1]
